title: Measuring Above-ground Biomass with Drone Photogrammetry: Data Collection Protocol
protocol: Survey extents will depend on the size and distribution of harvest plots.
Expect extents to range from 0.25 ha (50 m x 50 m) to 1 ha (100 m x 100 m) per site.
Identify community within harvest patches to the taxonomic level of family or plant functional type when dealing with mixed floristic communities in grasslands.
Prepare 13 ground control markers for each site.
Ensure each marker measures ≥ 20 cm x 20 cm.
Design markers with black and white segments.
Facilitate precise detection of the centre point.
Manufacture markers using printed corriboard or PTFE plastic plates.
Obtain markers from sign printing shops if necessary.
Include pre-drilled holes at the corners for anchoring with pegs.
Deploy 13 markers evenly across the survey site.
Ensure markers include the edges and several are in the center of the site.
Peg down all markers securely to prevent movement.
Geolocate each marker using survey-grade GNSS equipment for subcentimeter accuracy.
Avoid using low-precision GNSS units (±1 m) for this application.
Consider using consumer drones equipped with high-precision direct georeferencing systems for accurate image capture position measurements.
Demarcate a polygon around the site using coordinates or positioning the powered aircraft at each vertex.
Enter appropriate survey parameters into the app as recommended.
Review all mission parameters and ensure 'Waypoints Qty' ≤ 99.
Check that the area of interest is correct on the app.
Note that if estimated flight time exceeds the aircraft endurance, pause the survey to change the battery.
Specify or verify camera settings using the DJI Go App immediately before flights.
Ensure shutter speed is sufficiently fast to avoid motion blur \(ideally ≤1/800th second).
Adjust aperture or sensor sensitivity as necessary to optimize camera settings.
Set the camera’s target exposure to underexpose by -⅓ to -½ of a stop to optimize image quality.
Confirm that the camera angle is set correctly using manual gimbal control.
Select biomass harvest area(s) in agreement with landowners and other stakeholders.
Undertake an aerial survey as described above.
Review the acquired image dataset to ensure that images are of good quality, with no blurring or exposure issues.
Record detailed notes about the harvest site.
Select appropriate dimensions for the harvest plots.
Ensure harvest plots are ≥ 50 cm x 50 cm in area, ideally square.
Increase plot sizes in increments of 0.1m as needed.
In ecosystems with discrete plant individuals, ensure plots encompass entire plant individuals.
For ecosystems with coalesced plant individuals, plots should represent a sample of canopy and stems.
Adjust dimensions for small plants to be as small as 50 cm x 50 cm if applicable.
Document the dimension used for each plot.
Select individual harvest plots to include representative samples of small, medium, and large individuals for each (co-)dominant species.
Survey the corners of harvest plots with high-precision GNSS at ground surface level.
Measure corner coordinates sequentially around the plot either clockwise or counterclockwise.
Take three photographs of each harvest plot using a digital camera.
Photograph the plot ID code as the first photo.
View and photograph the plot from any direction as the second photo.
View and photograph the plot from a perpendicular direction as the third photo.
Clip all standing biomass within the harvest area to ground level.
Collect clipped vegetation directly into study paper bags or sheeting on the ground.
Exclude parts of plants that originate within the plot but extend beyond its edges from collection.
Include parts of plants that grow into the plot from outside in the collected material, if applicable.
Use a rigid frame to assist in identifying which parts of plants lie within plot boundaries during harvest.
Oven dry harvested material at 80°C for a minimum of 48 hours.
Ensure oven temperature does not exceed 80°C to avoid burning samples.
Perforate succulent plants prior to drying if necessary.
Retain representative sub-samples of dried matter for carbon content analysis.
Store three, approximately 10 g subsamples from each partition for further analysis.
